study type: Secondary analysis of cross-sectional surveys with meta-analysis
cohort: Women aged 15-49 years with a singleton live last birth during the 2 years preceding the survey from 33 low-income and middle-income countries in sub-Saharan Africa.
finding: Caesarean section was found to have a significant negative influence on the early initiation of breastfeeding across sub-Saharan Africa, but showed little association with exclusive breastfeeding under 6 months and children ever breastfed.
mod_finding: Compared with vaginal birth, meta-analysis indicated caesarean section was associated with a 46% lower prevalence of early initiation of breastfeeding, but little association with exclusive breastfeeding under 6 months and children ever breastfed.
followup_time: up to 6 months for exclusive breastfeeding (and up to 2 years for children ever breastfed, though the specific measurement timing isn't fixed at 2 years)
